bill.title: A resolution condemning Hamas for its premeditated, coordinated, and brutal terrorist attacks on October 7, 2023, against Israel and demanding that Hamas immediately release all remaining hostages and return them to safety, and for other purposes.
bill.latestActionText: Placed on Senate Legislative Calendar under General Orders. Calendar No. 101.
bill.officialSummary: This resolution condemns Hamas in the harshest terms for its attacks on Israel and demands that Hamas immediately release all remaining hostages. The resolution also (1) expresses sympathy to the hostages, those wounded, and their families; and (2) mourns those killed by Hamas on October 7, 2023, and during captivity.

classification.plainSummary: This resolution formally condemns Hamas for its October 7, 2023, attacks on Israel and demands the immediate release of all hostages still held. It expresses sympathy for hostages, the wounded, and their families, and mourns those killed during the attacks and in captivity. As a resolution, it records the Senate's position but does not change U.S. law or create new obligations.

plain.whatItDoes: This resolution would condemn Hamas in the harshest terms for its attacks on Israel and demand that Hamas immediately release all remaining hostages.
plain.whoItTouches: Mostly people outside the United States. It reaches most readers here only indirectly.
plain.everydayEffect: If it passed, the change would show up in what the United States does abroad. Nothing has changed yet. This kind of resolution does not become law, even if it passes.
plain.source: Reworded from the official summary. Staff at the Congressional Research Service wrote that summary. It is public domain, and the full text of it is further down this page.

disclaimer: This tool places two public records next to each other: who donated to a member of Congress, and what that member legislated on. Any overlap you see is a correlation, not causation. It is not evidence of a quid pro quo, of influence, or of wrongdoing. Legislators routinely receive support from industries in their district for the same reason they legislate on them: those industries are there.
